topic: Honest limitations and the state of the art at 2026-09-29
method_notes: All pages were fetched from the Higgsfield sandbox (open internet) and every quote was machine-checked as a substring of the fetched page text (whitespace and typographic quotes normalised; PDFs via pdftotext; JS-only pages such as kling.ai release notes and BytePlus docs via headless Chromium; X post timestamps via the syndication endpoint). A few quotes were checked in raw HTML for metadata dates. Where a quote differs from page text only by a stripped-link space (for example "web ," in help pages), the text is present on the page. openai.com and help.openai.com are cited as Wayback id_ captures (redirects resolve to the nearest capture shown in each URL). Sibling files R1-R4 were used as leads and every claim restated here was re-fetched by R6; items R6 did not re-fetch are labelled in notes or unverified_leads. Commons frames were not viewed.

corrections_to_common_beliefs: Sora was not released in February 2024: that was a research preview for red teamers and selected creatives. The public product arrived on 2024-12-09 as a different, faster model (Sora Turbo) capped at 20 seconds and 1080p; the "up to a minute" line was a capability claim, not something users got.

Sora is now discontinued: the web/app ended 2026-04-26 and the Sora 2 models and Videos API were shut down on 2026-09-24; OpenAI's docs say no one-to-one replacement API exists. Sora 2 must not be shown as an available or current model.

Sora 2 did not introduce sound in AI video: Veo 3 generated video and audio together on 2025-05-20, four months earlier, and Meta's Movie Gen research (2024-10-04) already produced synced audio (no public release).

Google's newest video model on 2026-09-29 is Gemini Omni (Flash 2026-05-19; 1.1 Flash 2026-08-27), not Veo 3. Veo 3.1 (2025-10-15) is the last named Veo and Google says Omni replaces Veo in the Gemini app, although DeepMind's Veo page still calls Veo 3.1 its leading Veo model. No Veo 4 exists in primary sources.

Google 1080p/4K is described as upscaling: the Omni API marks 1080p and 4K as "upscaled", and a Jan 2026 Veo 3.1 post says upscaling to 1080p and 4K is offered only in Flow, the Gemini API and Vertex AI (the Veo API doc separately says the model can "directly generate" these sizes). Avoid claiming native 4K.

Kling 4.0 is only announced (2026-09-28): Flash tier is limited early access for Ultra Yearly subscribers, full launch is promised for October 2026, and HDR and 2-minute extension are marked "coming soon". The newest generally available Kling models are 3.0 and 3.0 Turbo.
"Hailuo 3" is a third-party alias; MiniMax's own name for the 2026-07-31 model is MiniMax H3. Hailuo 02 (2025-06-18) and 2.3 (2025-10-28) are the earlier named versions.

Runway's flagship is not "Gen-5": its API docs name Gen-4.5 (announced 2025-12-01, paid plans 2025-12-11) and Aleph 2.0 (2026-05-21) as flagship models, and Ruby (2026-08-20) is an SDR-to-HDR grading model. Runway and Pika (verified on their own pages) and, per R3, Luma and Adobe now host other companies' models, so an app name does not identify the underlying model.

Long clips usually come from extension or shot stitching, not one long generation: Omni reaches 40 s by 10-second extension steps, Nova Reel's two minutes are 6-second shots, and Veo 3.1 clips are 8 s. Single-pass 30 s claims (Seedance 2.5, Wan3.0, Kling 4.0 Flash) are developer statements.
Runway's Gen-4.5 "#1" rank is a developer-cited benchmark snapshot dated at announcement, not a current or independent ranking; benchmark claims must not be repeated as scores in the film.
"Anyone could try it by 2023" is only true from June 2023 (Runway Gen-2 on web and iOS, "try it free"); in March 2023 Gen-2 was Discord early access and Pika 1.0 was a waitlist in November 2023.

Developers themselves state remaining flaws in 2025-2026: physics and causality (OpenAI, Runway), warped fingers and garbled text (Kling, Google Veo 2/3), identity drift across shots (Kling), text rendering and multi-subject consistency (Seed, Google, Alibaba), audio glitches (Seed, Google, Meta). Demo clips are curated selections.

Public-domain tags on Commons AI videos are PD-algorithm community assertions (US-centred; UK and Hong Kong protect computer-generated works for 50 years per the template), not developer licences, and several files are YouTube/X re-uploads. Commons has no footage from Kling, Wan, Runway Gen-4/4.5, Luma Ray3.x, Omni, MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.5.

Provenance is layered: Google embeds invisible SynthID plus C2PA metadata and can add a visible watermark in the Gemini app; OpenAI's Sora carried C2PA plus a visible (moving, in the app) watermark; Runway says it implements C2PA. Excerpts that keep a watermark must not be cropped away in vertical reframing.

evidence.claim: Video Diffusion Models (arXiv, 7 Apr 2022): first results on a large text-conditioned video generation task.
evidence.quote: We present the first results on a large text-conditioned video generation task

evidence.claim: CogVideo (arXiv, 29 May 2022): text-to-video model, open-sourced.
evidence.quote: As (probably) the first open-source large-scale pretrained text-to-video model, CogVideo outperforms all publicly available models at a large margin

evidence.claim: Google: Phenaki, arXiv 5 Oct 2022.

"Labs showed" is accurate; do not say "released" or "anyone could use" for 2022.
